original_question: Are the ERCC8 and ERCC6 genes located on the same chromosome?

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the ERCC8 gene located?
final_qi.long_answer: The ERCC8 gene, which encodes the Cockayne syndrome A (CSA) protein involved in transcription-coupled DNA repair, is mapped to the long arm of human chromosome 5 (cytogenetic band 5q12.1).

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the ERCC6 gene located?
final_qi.long_answer: In humans, the ERCC6 gene (also known as the Cockayne syndrome group B gene, CSB) is mapped to the long arm of chromosome 10 at band q11.23. This chromosomal assignment has been confirmed by linkage analysis and fluorescence in-situ hybridization studies.
